Explanation from 2023:
https://data.public.lu/fr/strategy/

o PSI: public sector institutions are invited to make their data available as much as possible, and to profit from existing open data.
o Metadata: an important factor in the open data project is the availability of complete and normalized metadata.
o Infrastructure: Central platform – decentralised data : Datasets are to be made available online by the data producers, either at their own websites or at the level of the national open data portal http://data.public.lu, where all existing data should be registered. o Searchability: quality and precision of the tags assigned to the data sets allow for a focused search.

Like the European Interoperability Framework, the National Interoperability Framework https://mindigital.gouvernement.lu/fr/dossiers/2019/NIF-2019.html  adopted in 2019 by the Luxembourg government covers open data by its very first principle “openness”. Under the principle of openness, this strategic document recommends to “Publish own data as open data by default, unless restrictions (security, data protection, etc.) apply”.
The open data team also contributes to the Ministry for Digitalisation’s three call for projects aimed at government administrations and services: NIF4Gov to further develop interoperability in the public sector domain; DATA4Gov to promote the use of data within the public sector; as well as,  AI4Gov to foster the use of artificial intelligence within the public sector. All three subject matters benefit greatly from an open data approach.
An important aspect is the consistent professional training for public sector employees, to help them be more aware of open data topics and become an active part in the open data ecosystem.
It should also be mentioned that the Ministry for Digitalisation works on several national projects - in collaboration with the open data team as well as the Luxembourg National Data Service (LNDS) - that are important contributions to the open data strategy:
- a national general data strategy is being finalised and due for publication soon. The data strategy reiterates the National Interoperability Framework’s approach of openness by default.
- a common and generalised data inventory effort is ongoing, together with the open data team at SIP, the above mentioned LNDS and all the other public sector organisations that work on cataloguing data: national library BNL, university and national archive etc

There is a 3 tier approach to achieve good or at least continuously better public sector open data quality in Luxembourg : 
- the first concerns chapters dedicated to public sector open data, the national portal, and related topics in the regular trainings proposed to any public sector agent at the training institute INAP
- the second is the (recently built) group of open data representatives at the public sector organisations. This group has been mentioned in other questions above, and has been created following the Prime Minister's order to officially name such representatives, in his letter https://data.public.lu/fr/datasets/lettre-circulaire-aux-departements-ministeriels-administrations-et-services-de-letat-donnees-ouvertes/ , where several practical measures have been outlined to fulfill the obligations of the open data directive and corresponding national laws. The idea behind this permanent group is to intensify exchanges, best practices, technical help and general open data related information between the responsible persons via regular meetings. The first meeting of this series has taken place in April 2024 https://data.public.lu/fr/posts/le-premier-open-data-meetup-du-gouvernement/
- the third is the 1-to-1 approach we already mentioned before : the open data team usually is in touch with each individual data owner and helps with advice or technical assistance when data is published. Due to this good connection to the data owners, we are able to help focussing on quality aspects like updates, resource formats, problems in the data itself, metadata etc. This has proven to be of great value for the general data quality on the portal. In this context we should name our link checking programme : To avoid presenting data which is not available anymore, we have automated tests in place to check the availability of data, for all the data which is not hosted directly on the portal. Every month, an automatic check is conveyed, which is filtered manually to avoid false positives, then the team of the open data portal contacts all the organisations which have an availability issue (dead links), and try to find a solution with them to have the data back online as soon as possible. It can range from simple url fixes to more complex operations such ass setting up an automated synchronisation with the open data portal. This has been the case for example with our national weather data provider, Meteolux:

In the portal, the internal statistic dashboard which renders key information about every dataset, is a good way to track the popularity of datasets, from the perspective of the data producers.
We keep an eye on the exchanges between data users and providers in the corresponding portal sections, to deduce possibly interesting re-use cases, and - as far as possible with the available means - we try to know more in order  to properly document the re-use to evaluate it's impact as well as to use it as an example to trigger further visibility for open data.
A particular case are API's where it is possible to require the use of a personal key, which obliges re-users to  be identified and the data providers to get detailed information about the uses. We have been able to detect and document reuses on this topic:
- https://data.public.lu/fr/reuses/tableaux-interactifs-sur-les-demandeurs-demploi-inscrits-a-ladem/ These are dashboards about unemployment in Luxembourg with lots of details, and the evolution of some data is also available. They have been developed by the public sector. They show that the category "IT systems and telecommunication" is one of the most important categories in terms of job offers. This information helped the Education ministry to develop a new concept of professional training in this domain, with the initiative DLH (digital learning hub) which started in 2022. The goal of DLH is to assist persons in  their professional transition to software development and other IT skills. It has been a great success, and an additional training institue  "42Luxembourg" has been created https://42luxembourg.lu/ which is an example of PPP.
- https://data.public.lu/fr/reuses/unemployment-luxembourg-facilitons-lemploi-chiffres-cles/ this dashboard is quite similar but maybe more synthetic and has been developed by a private sector company.
Both reuses are based on the same datasets.
